trial_court: Principal Judge Family Court, Singrauli (M.P.) as MJCR No. 120/2018

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: BHAGWANDAS S/O TILAKDHARI SHAH, AGED ABOUT 35 YEARS, OCCUPATION: LABOUR R/O VILL. DEVRA POST PANCHORE P.S. WAIDHAN DISTT. SINGRAULI M.P.
parties.respondent_defendant: PANPATI SHAH W/O BHAGWANDAS SHAH, AGED ABOUT 27 YEARS, OCCUPATION: HOUSE WIFE R/O VILL. DEVRA POST PANCHORE P.S. WAIDHAN DISTT. SINGRAULI M.P.

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married in 2017. The wife filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. claiming maintenance from the husband. The trial court partly allowed the application, directing the husband to pay Rs.10,000/- per month to the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The scope of Section 125 of Cr.P.C. cannot be enlarged to include a woman who is not lawfully married.
legal_principles.held: Even if the husband is treating the applicant as his wife, it is the intention of the legislature which is relevant and not to the attitude of the party.
cited_cases: Savitaben Somabhai Bhatiya vs. State of Gujarat & Ors., (2005) II MPWN 15=2005 AIR SCW 1601

legal_principles.principle: The revisional court has no power to reassess evidence and substitute its own findings in a maintenance order passed under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: In a revision against the maintenance order passed in proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C., the revisional court has no power to reassess evidence and substitute its own findings.
cited_cases: Suresh Mandal vs. State of Jharkhand, (2006) 1 AIR Jhar R 153

outcome.final_order: The petitioner's appeal against the impugned order was dismissed and the trial court's direction for maintenance was upheld.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
